seoTitle: Free Cyclomatic Complexity Estimator for JavaScript Functions
metaDescription: Estimate McCabe complexity per JavaScript function from pasted code. Flags functions above your limit. Heuristic, free, offline.
intro: Finds functions, methods and arrow functions in pasted JavaScript and estimates each one's cyclomatic complexity: one plus the number of if, for, while, case, catch, &&, ||, ?? and ternary operators inside it.
why:
Cyclomatic complexity is a rough count of independent paths through a function. High values mean more tests and more places for bugs. Linters report it, but only inside a project with a config.

This tool gives a quick estimate for a pasted file. It is a text scanner, not a parser, so odd syntax can fool it, and optional chaining and default values are not counted. Treat flagged functions as "review", and use a real linter in your build.
howTo: Set the level above which a function is flagged.
Read the list of functions and their scores.
Split or simplify the ones marked REVIEW.

faq.a: if, for (including in and of), while, case, catch, &&, ||, ?? and the ?: operator, plus one for the function itself.

faq.q: Are nested functions included in the outer score?
faq.a: No. Each function is scored on its own, like common linters do.
Many teams use 10 to 15. It is a convention, not a rule.
Simple cases may work, but types are not understood.
